chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Zurarah, from one of the two عليهما السلام, who said:

“The woman in postnatal bleeding refrains from salat for the number of days she used to remain thus, then she performs ghusl just as the woman with istihadah performs ghusl.” And she prays. If the blood passes through the cotton, she binds herself and performs ghusl, then prays the morning prayer with one ghusl, the zuhr and the 'asr with one ghusl, and the maghrib and the 'isha' with one ghusl. If it does not pass through the cotton, she prays with one ghusl.” I said: And the menstruating woman? He said: “That is the same equally. If the blood stops from her, otherwise she is a woman with istihadah: she does the same as the woman in postnatal bleeding exactly, then she prays and does not leave salat in any condition, for the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: ‘Salat is the pillar of your religion.’”

key_terms.الْكُرْسُفَ: cotton used to check or contain blood flow
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةُ: a woman experiencing irregular non-menstrual bleeding

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhib al-Ahkam say about salat and ghusl for nifas, hayd, and istihadah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings for women experiencing postnatal bleeding, menstruation, and istihadah in relation to salat and ghusl. It explains when salat is suspended, when ghusl is required, and emphasizes that ongoing non-menstrual bleeding does not permit abandoning salat.
